title: Planetary Migration, Resonances and System Architecture: Orbital Evolution, Tidal and Disc-Torque Budgets Against Energy and Density Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Rami Habib, and this is Planetary Migration, Resonances and System Architecture: Orbital Evolution, Tidal and Disc-Torque Budgets Against Energy and Density Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Rami Habib, and this is Planetary Migration, Resonances and System Architecture: Orbital Evolution, Tidal and Disc-Torque Budgets Against Energy and Density Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'GJ 876 and the Laplace Resonance: Three-Planet Libration, Torques and Tidal Damping'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): innermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.13094; innermost_migration_timescale_yr = 162.60998633785346; outermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.336768; outermost_migration_timescale_yr = 12869.011767814694; max_abs_period_ratio_deviation_percent = 1.716; total_orbital_energy_J = -4.528258500172236e+36.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'HD 110067: A Six-Planet Resonant Chain and Its Undisturbed Migration History'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): innermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.079204; innermost_migration_timescale_yr = 18643.590715912087; outermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.261799; outermost_migration_timescale_yr = 23000.45189447677; max_abs_period_ratio_deviation_percent = 11.113; total_orbital_energy_J = -5.7550245608529045e+35.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): innermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 14.539748; innermost_migration_timescale_yr = 2336.447429239774; outermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 34.595637; outermost_migration_timescale_yr = 5690.571639671004; max_abs_period_ratio_deviation_percent = 44.481; total_orbital_energy_J = -2.4365551474699926e+36.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Jupiter and the Grand Tack: Disc Torque Reversal, Migration Distance and Energy Budget'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): innermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 5.201211; innermost_migration_timescale_yr = 2484.47213596176; outermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 9.537913; outermost_migration_timescale_yr = 11231.183221880738; max_abs_period_ratio_deviation_percent = 0.669; total_orbital_energy_J = -1.8830663017823467e+35.

Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): innermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.09145; innermost_migration_timescale_yr = 73540.54238739383; outermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.465615; outermost_migration_timescale_yr = 63056.83105468402; max_abs_period_ratio_deviation_percent = 15.485; total_orbital_energy_J = -3.943233464047151e+35.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “GJ 876 and the Laplace Resonance: Three-Planet Libration, Torques and Tidal Damping”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): innermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.13094; innermost_migration_timescale_yr = 162.60998633785346; outermost_semi_major_axis_AU = 0.336768; outermost_migration_timescale_yr = 12869.011767814694; max_abs_period_ratio_deviation_percent = 1.716; total_or (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'GJ 876 and the Laplace Resonance: Three-Planet Libration, Torques and Tidal Damping'; 'HD 110067: A Six-Planet Resonant Chain and Its Undisturbed Migration History'; 'HR 8799: Four Massive Planets in Resonance, Libration and Long-Term Stability Budgets'; 'Jupiter and the Grand Tack: Disc Torque Reversal, Migration Distance and Energy Budget'; 'K2-138: A Near-Resonant Chain of Sub-Neptunes and Its Torque History'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
